Problem statement:
# Binary Search

Given a sorted array of `n` distinct integers and an integer `target`, find the index of the target using Binary Search.

Print the 0-based index if the target exists; otherwise, print `-1`.

### Input Format
- First line: Integer `n`.
- Second line: `n` space-separated integers in ascending order.
- Third line: Integer `target`.

### Output Format
Print the index of the target or `-1`.
### Constraints
- 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000
- -10⁹ ≤ arr[i], target ≤ 10⁹
- All array elements are distinct and sorted.

### Sample Input
```text
5
1 3 5 7 9
7
```

### Sample Output
```text
3
```

Sample 1 input:
```
5
1 3 5 7 9
7
```
Sample 1 output:
```
3
```

Reference solution:
```c
/* Reference solution generated by the llm_tests analyzer (ollama qwen2.5-coder:3b,
   temperature 0, seed 42, attempt 3). It reproduces every sample in the rules;
   review it before trusting the tests computed from it. */
#include <stdio.h>

int binarySearch(long long arr[], int n, long long target) {
    int left = 0;
    int right = n - 1;

    while (left <= right) {
        int mid = left + (right - left) / 2; // Prevents overflow

        if (arr[mid] == target) {
            return mid;
        } else if (arr[mid] < target) {
            left = mid + 1;
        } else {
            right = mid - 1;
        }
    }

    return -1;
}

int main() {
    int n;
    scanf("%d", &n);

    long long arr[n];
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        scanf("%lld", &arr[i]);
    }

    long long target;
    scanf("%lld", &target);

    int result = binarySearch(arr, n, target);
    printf("%d\n", result);

    return 0;
}
```
